title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：pan　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pan 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the baker ① heated the pan that no customer in the bakery would have noted, and he said the heating was the whole of the week. The ② pan, meaning the pot itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; a pan, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ pan in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ pan at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A pan, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the baker said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pan was the whole of the matter, meaning the warmth and not the pot. The ⑥ pan, meaning the warmth and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; pan, he said, is either something you heat or the only word that means both a pot and a warmth. He said the warmth is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ pan had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ pan of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of noting; pan, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pan I remember is the pot noted in the bill, which closed in 1960 and is still noted as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ pan, my mother said in 1962, is the only pot that improves by being noted; every pan, she said, is a warmth that has agreed to look like a pot. She said the warmth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 锅；平底锅（指糕饼铺里每一口旁边的那一口）
B. n. 锅；平底锅（指那口锅本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：heat the pan 烧热这一口锅
D. n. 锅；平底锅（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 锅之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的锅之事）
F. n. 锅；平底锅（指账单里写到、被记下的那一口）
G. n. 锅、烟火（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 烟火（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: heated the pan that no customer in the bakery would have noted
The pan, meaning the pot itself and not the tray
the pan at the far oven
the pan was the whole of the matter
the pan had become a line in a bill
The pan of the whole thing
A pan, my mother said in 1962

answers.why: heat the pan 意为“烧热这一口锅”，1953 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记下的一口锅做了一遍。
pan 意为“锅；平底锅”，指那口锅本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
pan 意为“锅；平底锅”，指糕饼铺里每一口旁边的那一口，每一口旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
pan 意为“锅；平底锅”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pan 意为“锅、烟火”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这口烟火就是那件事的全部。
pan 意为“烟火”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那口锅，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pan 意为“锅；平底锅”，指账单里写到、被记下的那一口，到 1958 年这一口成了账单里的一行。
pan 意为“锅之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的锅之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的记下。
pan 意为“锅；平底锅”，我记得的是账单里记下过的那一口，1960 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一口。
pan 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，锅是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的锅。
